about: MUTATING — the first, and the only one (David, 2026-09-03; see _about). Runs the forge host's disk-floor-sweep.sh, whose mechanism is TWO passes in a fixed order. Pass 0 runs on EVERY invocation, floor or no floor, against the SYSTEM daemon's per-train boss-ci:<sha> images (sha-shaped tags only, so the stable bases are never candidates): it deletes any image whose TRAIN IS DONE according to the system of record (landed-train-shas.lib.sh reads BOSS_JOBS_URL for landed and abandoned trains), then anything the record cannot vouch for that is older than the age window (BOSS_CI_IMAGE_AGE_HOURS, 6h), always keeping the newest 3 (BOSS_CI_IMAGE_KEEP_NEWEST) whatever their age because a job starting right now pulls them; when the record cannot be read at all, the loop is the age window alone — an SoR outage weakens the pass, never the floor. Pass 1 runs only while free space on the root volume is below floor_gb, in order, stopping as soon as the floor is met: builder cache (all of it), dangling images, then registry-verified old tags (keep the N newest, verify each candidate is present in the registry before rmi). Never volumes or non-docker paths, by construction of the script; /opt (Forgejo's own data) is out of its reach entirely. floor_gb: this verb's default is 100, the same number the hourly disk-floor-sweep.timer runs with (Environment=BOSS_DISK_FLOOR_GB=100 in its unit) — deliberately above the locomotive's 70 GB refusal so a floor buys headroom above the one that strikes cars; the script's own bare default is 70. The script is named relative to the repo and resolved against the runner's own checkout (66077f9c); this verb is scoped to forge because only the forge has the docker daemon it sweeps. A run killed at OPS_TIMEOUT is safe: every remediation already applied stays applied, and the hourly timer finishes the job. Pass 0's outcome is on the packet as 'CI-image prune freed N MiB'; a FLOOR UNMET exit is non-zero and says how far short it stopped.
